utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we allow the Defence to call its next witness, I would like to deal already with one more item on our agenda, which is dealing with the Rule 92 bis motion related to the Prosecution's re-opening of its case. On the 6th of November of last year, the Prosecution tendered the evidence of five witnesses under Rule 92 bis as a -- as part of the re-opening of its case. On the 19th of November, the Defence asked for an extension of 30 days in which to file its response which the Chamber granted in full. On the 20th of November, the Chamber set a new deadline of the 22nd of December. However, the Defence did not filing its response until the 29th of December, having missed the deadline by a full week without requesting a further extension or making any submissions in its response as to why the Chamber should accept its late filing. The Chamber is concerned about the -- this lack of diligence on the part of the Defence. Considering the importance of the matter, however, the Chamber, pursuant to Rule 127, exceptionally accepts the Defence response as timely filed. In addition, the Prosecution sought leave to reply on the 5th of January of this year. The Chamber grants the Prosecution leave to reply and will consider the reply submitted by the Prosecution. In footnote 8 of its filing, the Prosecution submits that it recently received Rule 92 bis certifications for the tendered material and that it will disclose these to the Defence in the near future. As the Rule 92 bis verifications are a requirement for admission, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to file them on the record as opposed to only disclosing them to the Defence. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness, which will give his testimony in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 22nd of January, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning, and the Chamber expects that it will be in closed session for the first -- at least the first half of tomorrow's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
